text.p: Eagle-Picher Industries said Monday that the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Cincinnati entered an order confirming the company's third amended consolidated plan of reorganization.
The plan was filed jointly by the company, the Injury Claimants' Committee (ICC) and the Representative for Future Claimants (RFC), a statement from Eagle-Picher said.
The company said the ICC represents about 150,000 people alleging injury due to exposure to asbestos-containing products manufactured by Eagle-Picher from 1934 until 1971.
Future personal injury claimants are represented by the RFC, Eagle-Picher said.
The Unsecured Creditors' Committee appointed in the chapter 11 cases also supported confirmation of the plan, the company said.
The company said the total amount of claims is $2.157 billion.

Of that amount $2.0 billion is for the company's liability with respect to present and future asbestos-related personal injury claims. The company said all other prepetition claims add up to about $157 million.

"The company is going to exchange cash, notes and stock to discharge all prepetition claims," company spokesman David Hall told Reuters in a telephone interview. "The unsecured creditors who make up the $157 million will receive half cash and half three-year notes equaling 37 percent of their claims."
The company said all present and future asbestos and lead-related personal injury claims will be channeled to a trust which will resolve and satisfy all such claims.
The company said the reorganized Eagle-Picher will enjoy a positive net worth of about $340 million.
